build: lean and muscular from years of studio work, shoulders broad from repetitive motion
hair: black, thick and straight, worn in a high bun during work; falls past her shoulders when loose
complexion: warm brown with golden undertones; a small scar above her left cheekbone from a childhood fall on ice
face: a wide, open face with high cheekbones and deep-set dark eyes that telegraph every emotion before her mouth catches up—the kind of face that cannot lie, that reads as startled or hungry or furious in real time
signature_feature: her hands—long-fingered, scarred from glasswork, with a particular steadiness when she's concentrating that makes watching her work feel like witnessing ritual
second_celebrated_feature: the hollow at the base of her throat, visible when she pulls her hair back, that catches light and draws the eye downward
signature_habits: she hums while working—old Inuit throat-singing fragments her grandmother taught her, wordless and rhythmic; she touches her collarbone when nervous, a grounding gesture; she keeps a small tupilak carving on her studio shelf and runs her thumb over it before major commissions; she drinks strong black tea obsessively, always too hot
occupation: glass artist and studio owner—bespoke sculptural pieces and architectural installations for high-end residential and commercial clients in the billionaire_modern sphere

current_crisis.event: a major collector and patron who funds 40% of her studio's annual revenue has suddenly demanded she produce a series of pieces in six weeks that directly contradicts her artistic vision and process; refusal means financial collapse; acceptance means compromising the only thing that feels true
current_crisis.immediate_want: to call someone and have them tell her it will be okay, but there is no one to call

wound.core: she believes that needing anyone—financially, emotionally, creatively—is a form of drowning; independence is survival
wound.surfacing_hint: when forced to ask for help or admit vulnerability, her voice becomes very small and her eyes go wet before she catches herself and hardens
